title: Mental accounting: why IDCW feels good
objectives: Explain mental accounting and why payouts feel like income while SWPs feel like touching capital.
Say why the economics are the same and where SWP still wins.
body_md:
Mental accounting: why IDCW feels good. People tend to treat money differently depending on which “mental account” it sits in. A payout feels like income, so investors are happy to spend it, while selling units in an SWP feels like “touching the capital”. Economically, the two are the same: both take money out of the fund. The difference is tax and control, and on both counts an SWP usually wins.

> **Talk-track:** “Whether the fund sends you money or you take it out yourself, it comes from the same place. The SWP just lets you choose the amount and pay less tax.”

> **Investor takeaway:** Don't judge a fund by its payouts. Judge it by its total return, after tax.
example: Payout ₹25,000 feels like income; SWP ₹25,000 feels like touching capital — economically both take ₹25,000 out of the fund; the SWP just lets you choose the amount and pay less tax.
say: Both take money out of the same place; SWP gives control and usually less tax.
Judge a fund by total return, after tax — not by payouts.
never: A payout and an SWP are economically different in amount.
SWPs always cost more tax than IDCW.
